collection.description: Children invent a game where nobody can win alone: teach it to everyone, or keep it for the children.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) have invented a game where everyone is tied together by vines, and the team only wins if nobody falls over. Nobody can win alone. The children love it. The adults are curious. What should the children do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The children teach the adults. The adults are terrible at it. The elders are worse. By the end of the festival, the whole village is tied together in one enormous, wobbling line, and nobody falls over, and the cheer can be heard across the bay.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The children keep it to themselves, and play it every evening on the beach. The adults watch from a distance, very curious. It becomes the children's game, passed down from child to child, and no adult ever quite learns the rules.
